note: cells that must stay green (runner 740c05a). K3 task 18 full matrix 2026-10-08 (runs 20261008-0448..0812 JVM image, 0751..0905 native image as kuicksilver-native): every cell green in the final state of the JVM matrix (18 cases × 6 peers × 2 roles) and of the native subset (handshake, transfer, retry, keyupdate, ecn, rebind-port × 5 peers); red cells and why are in docs/spec/rfc-compliance.md «Interop-матрица K3». Not required (known runner artefact, ~1 run in 3): the picoquic rebind cells — when the simulator's first rebind at 1 s lands inside the handshake, picoquic answers the handshake-time PATH_CHALLENGE coalesced behind a Handshake packet and the runner's check (first QUIC layer only) misses the PATH_RESPONSE; the server behaviour is pinned by core.PathTest (natRebindDuringHandshake*). K5: the http3 case (runs 20261008-160445 JVM image, 20261008-160623 native image): every peer that supports it in the runner (ngtcp2, picoquic, quic-go, quiche, quinn; msquic does not) green in both roles with both images. Not required since 2026-10-09 (owner decision, 0.1.0): the server-role handshakecorruption cells — with an ML-KEM client both flights span two datagrams, and under the scenario's 30 % drop the RFC 9002 initial PTO (1 s, 2 s, 4 s) gives three retransmissions before the peer client's 10 s handshake timeout (ngtcp2, quic-go, quiche); the client-role cells stay required (the interop client waits 30 s). 0.2.0: configurable initialRtt. Also not required since 2026-10-09 (peer behaviour under the simulator, run 20261009-040848): kuicksilver->msquic:amplificationlimit — msquic reads our three-datagram first flight in one batch, answers with one coalesced ACK datagram and then probes once per PTO, so its eighth datagram (the first the scenario lets through) comes after its own handshake timeout in about half of the runs (3 of 8 green); msquic->kuicksilver:rebind-addr — when the simulator's rebind at 1 s drops msquic's PATH_CHALLENGE to the new address, msquic retransmits the challenge only to the old address while sending data to the new one, stays amplification-limited there and idles out; the client never sees a challenge to answer (4 of 6 green). Also not required since 2026-10-09 (msquic under the simulator, runs 20261009-152351 and the rerun after it): msquic->kuicksilver:rebind-port — the runner requires the server's first packet on a new path to carry PATH_CHALLENGE, and msquic's first packet after the third rebind is an ACK (our client answered every challenge msquic did send) — re-read on 2026-10-17: that packet is ACK + CONNECTION_CLOSE, msquic's RFC 9000 10.2 answer to our client's CONNECTION_CLOSE, which the rebind at 11 s made the first packet from the new port (tools/interop/closing-rebind.py; the same in 20261008-003423 rebind-addr); msquic->kuicksilver-native:rebind-port stays required: its transfer ended at about 11 s since the clients start after the first rebind, and 0.2.0 gate 6 hit it (run 20261017-054938), so run-local.sh classifies that signature as ENVIRONMENT and reruns the cell; since 0.2.1 sim-entrypoint.sh opens the clients' port 1.25 s after the first rebind in rebind-port, so every client starts a second later and the transfers end between the rebinds at 11 s and 16 s (this cell at about 12.5 s), and the classifier stays as a backstop (rebind-addr keeps the earlier start: ngtcp2's server never receives from the simulator's binding of 11-16 s there); kuicksilver->msquic:rebind-addr — msquic's two-instance ClientHello (see handshakeloss) keeps the handshake in the Initial space and, when the rebind lands there, msquic answers the server's PATH_CHALLENGE in an Initial packet, which RFC 9000 section 12.4 forbids (our server closes with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION). K7 (2026-10-13, runs 20261013-034946..k7-pack, JVM and native images from k7/interop): resumption in both roles and zerortt in both roles against all six peers are required with both images, except quinn->kuicksilver[-native]:zerortt (the client's ACKs alone give 4.3–4.5 KB of the runner's 5000-byte 1-RTT budget); zerortt became green in the client role after two fixes on k7/interop (data and FIN in one STREAM frame for quiche's hq server; concurrent flushAndClose calls sharing packets so all 39 requests fit the initial window, runs k7-fix and k7-pack). With the native image quiche joins the subset: handshake, transfer and retry in both roles are required. The rest of the K7 matrix and the cells that stayed red are in docs/spec/rfc-compliance.md «Interop matrix K7». quic-go->kuicksilver:handshakecorruption stays required: it went red in 2 of 4 runs until a client endpoint started new connections from the last measured RTT to the same server (RFC 9002 6.2.2), then 6 of 6 green (docs/spec/rfc-compliance.md «Interop matrix K7»). kuicksilver->picoquic:v2 is not required (the picoquic defect in docs/spec/rfc-compliance.md) and ends at the runner's 60 s timeout; since 0.2.1 environment.sh does not take a runner timeout for an unflushed capture (the runner cut the output off and judged no capture), so run-local.sh no longer reruns it (0.2.0 gate, run 20261017-175019: rerun five times).
